## 8.2.1.1 Question 1

##### In real-world analysis, you would inspect all files, not just the first two. Make sure that your code chunk checks all forward and reverse files.

```{r}
# Load the library
library(dada2)
library(phyloseq)

data_dir <- here::here("data/MiSeq_SOP")

# Identify all forward and reverse FASTQ files
fnFs <- sort(list.files(
  data_dir,
  pattern = "_R1_001\\.fastq(\\.gz)?$",
  full.names = TRUE
))

fnRs <- sort(list.files(
  data_dir,
  pattern = "_R2_001\\.fastq(\\.gz)?$",
  full.names = TRUE
))

# Extract sample names
sample.names <- sub(
  "_R1_001\\.fastq(\\.gz)?$",
  "",
  basename(fnFs)
)

# Verify matching forward and reverse reads
stopifnot(length(fnFs) > 0)
stopifnot(length(fnFs) == length(fnRs))

# Plot quality profiles for ALL forward reads
plotQualityProfile(fnFs)

# Plot quality profiles for ALL reverse reads
plotQualityProfile(fnRs)
```


## 8.8.3 Question 2
##### Have a code chunk that generates the same output but for the reveres read.

```{r}
#| warning=FALSE
library(dplyr)

#Read trimming
#R1
filtFs <- here::here("outputs/filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_F_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtFs) <- sample.names
#R2
filtRs <- here::here("outputs/filtered", paste0(sample.names, "_R_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtRs) <- sample.names

out <- filterAndTrim(fnFs, filtFs, fnRs, filtRs, truncLen=c(240,160),
              maxN=0, maxEE=c(2,2), truncQ = 2 ,rm.phix=TRUE,
              compress=TRUE, multithread = TRUE)

out2 <- as.data.frame(out) %>% mutate(prop = (100*(reads.out/reads.in)))
head(out2)

# Learn error rates for forward and reverse reads
errF <- learnErrors(filtFs, multithread=T)
errR <- learnErrors(filtRs, multithread=T)

# Visualize the learned errors for the foward reads
plotErrors(errF, nominalQ=TRUE)

# Visualize the learned errors for the reverse reads
plotErrors(errR, nominalQ=TRUE)

# Export reverse-read error plot to PDF
pdf(
  here::here("outputs", "reverse_error_rates.pdf"),
  width = 8,
  height = 6
)

plotErrors(errR, nominalQ = TRUE)
```

##### Do you see similar results for the revers reads?
- Based on the observation between 2 graph, the reverse reads show a similar general trend, with error rates decreasing as quality scores increase. 
- However, reverse reads may have higher error rates or more variability than forward reads, particularly at lower quality scores, because reverse-read quality tends to decline toward the end of sequencing

```{r}
# 8.3.0.1 ASV inference

dadaFs <- dada(filtFs, err=errF, multithread = TRUE)
dadaFs
dadaRs <- dada(filtRs, err=errF, multithread = TRUE)
dadaRs

mergers <- mergePairs(dadaFs, filtFs, dadaRs, filtRs, verbose=TRUE)

# Inspect the merger data.frame from the first sample
DT::datatable(mergers$F3D0,options = list(scrollX = TRUE, autoWidth = TRUE))

seqtab <- makeSequenceTable(mergers)

dim(seqtab)

# ---------------------
# 8.3.2.1 Sanity checks are important

table(nchar(getSequences(seqtab)))

# 8.3.3 Chimera removal

seqtab.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab, method="consensus", multithread=F, verbose=TRUE)
#Proportion ASVs were removed due to chimeras?
100-(dim(seqtab.nochim)[2]/dim(seqtab)[2]*100)
sum(seqtab.nochim)/sum(seqtab)*100


# ---------------------
# 8.3.3.1 Read retention through the pipeline: final sanity check

getN <- function(x){ 
  sum(getUniques(x))
}

track <- cbind(out, sapply(dadaFs, getN), sapply(dadaRs, getN), sapply(mergers, getN), rowSums(seqtab.nochim))

colnames(track) <- c("input", "filtered", "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nonchim")
rownames(track) <- sample.names


# ---------------------
# 8.3.3.2 Data polishing part 1

ASV_tbl <- as.data.frame(seqtab.nochim) %>% 
  `colnames<-`(base::paste("ASV", seq(1:ncol(seqtab.nochim)), sep = ""))

DT::datatable(ASV_tbl, options = list(scrollX = TRUE, autoWidth = TRUE))



ASV_tbl <- as.data.frame(t(ASV_tbl[-nrow(ASV_tbl),]))

#lets remove the ASVs that were only present in the mock communities

ASV_tbl <- ASV_tbl %>% mutate(rs = rowSums(ASV_tbl)) %>% 
  filter(rs > 0) %>% dplyr::select(-rs)

library(Biostrings)
#Using DNAStringSet from Biostrings to read the seqs 
ASV_seqs <- DNAStringSet(base::colnames(seqtab.nochim) %>% 
                           `names<-`(base::paste("ASV",seq(1:ncol(seqtab.nochim)),sep = "")))


taxa <- assignTaxonomy(seqtab.nochim, here::here("data/silva_nr99_v138.1_wSpecies_train_set.fa.gz"), multithread=TRUE)


# ---------------------
# 8.3.4.1 Data polishing part 2

  `row.names<-`(base::paste("ASV", seq(1:nrow(taxa)), sep = ""))

DT::datatable(taxa2,options = list(scrollX = TRUE, autoWidth = TRUE))


taxa2 <- taxa2 %>% filter(Family != "Mitochondria") %>% filter(Order != "Chloroplast")

taxa3 <- taxa2 %>% mutate(ASVs = row.names(taxa2)) %>% dplyr::select(ASVs, everything())

taxa3 <- taxa3 %>% inner_join(ASV_tbl2, by = "ASVs")

taxa2 <- taxa2 %>% filter(rownames(taxa2)%in%taxa3$ASVs)
ASV_tbl <- ASV_tbl %>% filter(row.names(ASV_tbl) %in% taxa3$ASVs)

taxa3[,(ncol(taxa2)+2):ncol(taxa3)] <- sweep(
  taxa3[,(ncol(taxa2)+2):ncol(taxa3)],2,
  colSums(taxa3[,(ncol(taxa2)+2):ncol(taxa3)]),'/')*100

colSums(taxa3[,(ncol(taxa2)+2):ncol(taxa3)])

ASV_seqs[names(ASV_seqs)%in%ASV_tbl2$ASVs] 



# Find Firmicutes ASVs without genus and species assignments

  dplyr::filter(

firmicutes_candidates
actinobacteria_candidates

selected_seqs
```

```{r}
mdta

mdta <- mdta %>% mutate(category = if_else(dpw > 100 , "Late","Early")) %>%

  mutate(subject = str_extract(str_split_fixed(group, "D", 2)[,1],"(\\d)+")) %>%
  `row.names<-`(mdta$group)

all(colnames(ASV_tbl) == rownames(mdta))

ps <- phyloseq(otu_table(as.matrix(ASV_tbl), taxa_are_rows=T),

ps


# 8.4.1 Alpha diversity visualization

#Lets calculate richness and diversity
#Shannon and Simpson are diversity estimators, ACE is a richness estimator, observed is how many ASVs we have (198)
#Lets calculate richness and diversity
#Shannon and Simpson are diversity estimators, ACE is a richness estimator, observed is how many ASVs we have (198)
rnd <- estimate_richness(
  ps, measures=c("Observed", "ACE","Shannon", "Simpson")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-se.ACE)

DT::datatable(rnd[1:2])


DT::datatable(rnd[1:2])


# Export the alpha diversity table to a CSV file
write.csv( rnd, file = "alpha_diversity.csv", row.names = TRUE)
```

## 8.4.1.2 Question 5
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)

rnd <- rnd %>% mutate(group = row.names(rnd))%>% inner_join(mdta, "group")
#make a long table
rndl <- rnd %>% gather("Estimator", "Value", 1:4) %>% 
  mutate(rd = if_else(Estimator == "Observed" | Estimator == "ACE", 
                      "Richness","Diversity"))


# Create the improved plot with theme_bw() and a colorblind-friendly palette (e.g., "Set2" or "Dark2")
p <- ggplot(rndl, aes(x = dpw, y = Value, color = Estimator, fill = Estimator)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  facet_grid(rd ~ category, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +                                    # Sets the black and white theme
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2") +          # Colorblind-friendly color palette
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +           # Colorblind-friendly fill palette
  labs(title = "Species Richness and Diversity Estimates",
       x = "Days Past Weaning (dpw)",
       y = "Estimate Value")

# Display the plot in your knitted report
print(p)

# Save the plot as a PDF file in your project directory
ggsave("diversity_richness_plot.pdf", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6)
```
